Before we build anything

Snake is six
different games
and none of them
are pretty.

Eighteen of the biggest Snake games on iOS, read side by side. What each lane is actually doing, what they all copy from each other, and the four places nobody is standing.

Where it started 0000

01 — The board

Eighteen titles, ranked by review volume

Ratings count is the only public proxy for install scale, so treat these as orders of magnitude rather than gospel. The two numbers worth staring at: Snake Clash! put up 774k in three years while Snake.io took ten to reach 473k — and Snake VS Block, a single mechanic from 2017, is still within arm's reach of both.

02 — Six lanes

They share a name and almost nothing else

Search "snake" and the results look like one genre. They aren't. Six distinct games are wearing the same word, and they want completely different things from a player. The bar under each is the summed review volume of the titles in that lane — a rough measure of how much oxygen it takes up.

The .io arena

Slither.io's descendants, and the lane most people picture when they hear "modern snake". Top-down 2D, free-angle steering, boost by ejecting mass behind you, and you kill not by hitting someone but by making them hit you. Instant respawn, no fail screen worth the name. Money comes from rewarded-video revives, skin gacha and a battle pass.

Snake.io launched in April 2016 and shipped an update ten days before this scan. Netflix licensed it for their games tier. Kooapps run a second paid-tier build on Apple Arcade. This lane is defended.

764,001

The clash treadmill

The single biggest number on the board, and the newest thing that got there: 774,000 ratings in three years against Snake.io's 473,000 in ten. Supercent did not change the loop. They bolted a persistent level number onto the snake and a boss ladder onto the session — Lv 182 Player chasing BOSS Lv 1000 against a 1:23 clock.

That is the hybrid-casual playbook applied to snake: hypercasual session, meta-progression underneath it so the numbers keep climbing between runs. It is where the growth in this category currently lives.

773,920
US ratings across
scanned titles in lane

The 3D arena

Same loop, third-person camera, battle-royale framing. Boas.io has the best idea in the lane — you swallow a city, cars and buildings and whole blocks at a time, which is a genuinely funny escalation of "eat the pellet".

But 3D makes snake's central legibility problem worse rather than better. You cannot see your own tail, and your own tail is the thing that kills you. Note the ratings: the whole lane put together does not reach a fifth of Snake Clash!, and Snake Master 3D has not been touched since May 2021.

143,814
US ratings across
scanned titles in lane

The mechanic remix

Keep the one idea worth keeping — your body is your length — and throw the grid away completely. Length becomes ammunition fired at numbered blocks (Snake VS Block), a runner's queue of segments you gain and lose down a track (Snake Run Race), or a bullet-hell shooter where the tail is your health bar and your damage output at the same time (SSSnaker).

Best return on invention anywhere in this scan. Snake VS Block is one mechanic from a 2017 Voodoo prototype and it is still, nine years later, the second-biggest game on the board.

740,796
US ratings across
scanned titles in lane

The untangle puzzle

The current gold rush. No real-time skill at all: the snakes are knotted, and you tap them out in the order that lets each one leave without crossing another. Snake Escape launched in October 2025 and has 16,500 ratings at 4.79★ ten months later.

Worth being honest about what this is. Snake is a skin stretched over the unblock / tap-away puzzle template that is currently eating the casual puzzle charts — the same machine that produced Color Block Jam and Screwdom. Fast money, brutally crowded, and not really our game.

140,107
US ratings across
scanned titles in lane

The thinky grid puzzle

Deterministic, turn-based, one correct solution, no clock. This is the lineage that produced the genre's masterpiece — Snakebird, 85 on Metacritic — and it has, on iOS, the smallest audience here by two full orders of magnitude.

Snaggle is the one to sit with. A properly designed multi-snake path-drawing game, 4.83★ from the twenty-three people who found it, last updated March 2019. Highest craft on the board, no distribution, dead.

3,186
US ratings across
scanned titles in lane

The relic

Snake '97 renders the game inside a photographed Nokia bezel — 5110, 3210, 3310, 8210, 8850, 7110 — with the keypad attached and the monotone bleeps intact. Nine original difficulty levels, both Snake 1 and Snake 2, the labyrinths, going through the walls.

It is fifteen years old, rated 4.73★, and was updated this February. Nostalgia is a durable niche and it is already served perfectly. There is nothing to take here except the reminder that the monochrome screen is the only art direction in this whole scan that anybody remembers.

03 — Controls

Nobody has solved touch steering

Four control families are in active use, and every one of them trades away something the game needs.

Floating joystick + boost
Snake.io, Insatiable.io, SSSnaker. The most precise option, and it costs a thumb's worth of screen plus a handedness setting to make it work for everyone.
Drag-anywhere
Worms Zone, Little Big Snake. Nothing on screen but your snake — and your finger sits directly over the area you are steering into.
Swipe to turn
Snake Rivals classic, Snake VS Block. Lowest fidelity, highest accessibility, genuinely one-handed. Only works when the game is forgiving.
Tap to act
The untangle puzzles. No dexterity required at all, which is the entire proposition.

Here is the tell. Snake.io ships four control modes, plus left- and right-handed layouts, plus draggable placement for both the stick and the boost button. Ten years and 473,000 ratings in, the market leader still cannot pick one. That is not thoroughness — that is an unsolved problem with a settings menu bolted over it.

04 — The look

One art direction, eighteen times

Scroll back through the strips above and the sameness is hard to unsee: googly cartoon eyes on the head, segmented bead bodies, hexagonal or dotted grounds, a leaderboard pinned top-right with a crown on first place, and skins sorted into COMMON / RARE / EPIC / LEGEND / VIP. The store copy converges too — every listing screenshot carries an all-caps banner in a bright block colour.

Actual banner copy, verbatim, across the shortlist

Eat everything!Grow biggerKill snakes!Collect skinsMeet new friends!Become the best!Surround cityEat buildingsEliminate othersLast one standsGet longer!Won't be easyUntangle the snakesHelp them get freeWatch out for obstaclesTon of accessoriesEat & growSlither smartDodge trapsDon't get stuck!Brain test

Two listings look like they came from a different medium. Snake '97 renders the game inside a photographed Nokia bezel, monochrome, with the keypad still attached. SSSnaker spends Habby money on painted dungeon art. Everything else in between is the same sweet shop.

05 — The gap

Four places nobody is standing

Count is how many scanned titles occupy the space

1 of 18Nobody has made a beautiful one

The chart is candy-hypercasual at one end and literal Nokia nostalgia at the other, with nothing in the middle. There is no Monument Valley of snake, no Alto's Odyssey, no Threes! — no calm, crafted, aesthetically confident version of this game anywhere on the store. Snaggle reached for it in 2018, scored 4.83★ from its handful of players, and stopped shipping in March 2019.

0 of 18The grid has been abandoned

Everything modern steers on a free angle. The original's real pleasure — reading a lattice, planning three turns ahead, feeling a turn land on the beat — survives only in the tiny thinky-puzzle corner where it is turn-based and slow. A real-time snake that stays grid-locked, with input buffering good enough that a queued turn always lands, is not on this chart.

1 of 18Length is only ever a score

Almost every title treats length as a number that only goes up. Snake VS Block is the one game that lets you spend it, and it is the single biggest remix on the board. A snake where deliberately shedding length is a move — to fit a gap, to pay a cost, to reset a board — is an untapped vein sitting in plain sight.

0 of 18Two players, one device

For a lot of people the sharpest memory of Snake 2 is the infrared two-player match against the person sitting opposite. Nothing in this scan does same-device or same-room multiplayer. Every multiplayer game here is a lobby full of strangers and bots.

06 — Next

Four answers I need before scoping

Platform. Native iOS, or web-first and installable? Web is the faster path and matches what you already run. Native is the only route onto the charts above.

Purpose. Craft piece and portfolio, or is this meant to earn? It changes whether meta-progression gets built at all.

Which gap. The aesthetic one, the grid one, and the length-as-resource one point at three genuinely different games. Picking two is fine. Picking all four is not.

A name. For the game and for the repo.
